sections.h2: Gas's share of India's energy has slipped, not risen, since 2014-15

chart.title: Gas fell from 7.5% of primary energy in 2014-15 to 7.0% in 2023-24
chart.sub: Gas share of India's primary energy supply, %. Fiscal years.

sections.means: Gas use grew more slowly than total energy supply, so its share slipped over the decade.
sections.todo: Publish the yearly path the target implies, so progress against 15% can be measured.

sections.h2: A 15% share by 2029-30 would need 2.8 times the gas India used in 2025-26

chart.title: 15% of primary energy in 2029-30 means about 190 bcm of gas a year
chart.sub: Gas a year, billion cubic metres.
chart.source: This blog's arithmetic on MoSPI, PPAC and IEA figures.

sections.means: Almost all of the extra gas would have to be imported as LNG, at about 112 million tonnes a year.
sections.todo: Test the target against an import plan that India can actually finance.

sections.h2: Idle gas power plants are a small lever, running at about a tenth of capacity

chart.title: Gas power plants ran at 10.5% average load in 2025-26, against about 24% in 2017-18
chart.sub: Average load of India's gas-fired power fleet, %.

sections.means: Taking the fleet back to its 2017-18 load would add only about 1.0 percentage points to gas's share.
sections.todo: Use a flexible allocation framework so idle plants get gas at prices they can burn.

sections.h2: Terminals are not the bottleneck; pipelines and gas prices are

chart.title: Terminals ran at 47% of capacity in 2025, down from 58% in 2024

sections.means: The constraint is pipeline capacity to move gas inland and the price of the gas, not the tanks.
sections.todo: Prefer more pipeline out of existing terminals over new terminals.
